records.c: Build the shape number from the actor's animation selector. On a rare random result adjust Y by toggling bit one. The selector chooses left or right motion by one pixel, with a screen-boundary test.
While the slot's Y is at least $69, copy Arthur's X into the slot and move its Y up by one. Register the same position on the next update if Y remains at least $69.

On even phases advance X and test the bounds and the resident overlap routine. If Arthur overlaps, advance his X by one too. Call $8F68 using the slot flags and retire the slot if it reports carry set. Set shape $A2 and counter $FF on the surviving path.
Mark the slot inactive by storing $FF in its type.
Set flags to zero. The alternate entry points at $8778 and $877B set flags to four and sixteen.
Install the selected flags, a counter of four and type $49.
Choose a shape using two phase bits ORed with the variant flags. At Y=$8E, switch to type $4A when no other active slot has that type. Save the side of Arthur as a direction flag.
Use the direction flag to move X by one unit left or right. Deactivate the slot if X reaches $B0. Otherwise select its animation frame and call the common interaction helper.
Shape numbers indexed by the phase bits and type $49 flags. The indexes for flags $10 also reach the first four bytes at $87FF.
Left and right shape sequences read by $87DE using the current phase and direction. The final four bytes at $87FF also serve the type $49 variant with flags $10.
With zero delay, test for random value eight under mask $0F. On success change the type to $4D and allocate a type $4F slot.
Load base shape $B2. The entry at $8827 loads $B6. Both paths process the delay and direction bytes.
If either direction byte is nonzero, add the two bytes to the slot position. If both are zero, refresh the phase-dependent shape.
On one of four random outcomes, derive a delay from the vertical distance and another random sample. Select vertical step three and a horizontal step from zero, one and minus one using Arthur's X.
Move the slot up before animating it. On even phases use the movement index at $19B4 to select two signed offsets and advance the index. Selected indexes can restart motion selection.
Zero the horizontal step and select vertical step minus five. Derive a delay from the current Y and a random value, then switch to type $4E.
Check bounds and linked-slot state. If a companion index remains, place it 13 pixels below and two X units to the right of the current slot. Then enter the common interaction handler.
Add bits two and three of $BC to the base shape in $12.
Forty signed horizontal offsets used by $88D6 before the movement index reaches $28.
Forty signed vertical offsets paired with the X table and applied by $88E0.
Select shape $BA through the resident shape setter.
Set the hit counter to two and the motion index to $13 before advancing to type $51.

Alternate shapes $BB and $BC and apply paired X and Y deltas when $BB has its low bit set. Reset the index after twenty steps, add two to X and four to Y, then run the resident coordinate and hit checks.
Select shape $BD–$C0 by phase and set the slot's hit counter to $FF.
Set the IRQ operand to five, advance the actor type and set the hit counter to $14. Initialize the movement state using the difference from Arthur's X.
Patch both sprite descriptor bytes based on the slot's X relative to Arthur and alternate shapes $C1 and $C2. Dispatch motion according to the current state, then check hits with parameter $0E.
Compute a position from the current distance. Restore the saved coordinates with signed steps chosen by comparing them with the projection. Shrink the distance after each step.
Update the projected position and move the distance argument toward $2A on an angle boundary. At that distance, a random test can select one of two subsequent motion states.
State one uses a fixed step and reduces the distance after each angle boundary. State two uses Arthur's position as its origin and ramps the additional angle step up and down.
Run the standard hit check and retire through $3397 if the slot drops below type $53.
X step zero, minus two or plus two based on the difference from the projected position.
Y step zero, minus one or plus one based on relative height.
Live X origin added to the horizontal projection by $8B9C.
Live Y origin added to the vertical projection by $8BAE.
The additional angular step that rises and falls in the state-two update.
Zero while the extra step rises. The update decrements it to $FF to select the falling path.
The current movement state written here by the entry at $8A23.
Advance the angle by two and call the resident horizontal and vertical projection helpers. The vertical call uses twice the horizontal distance argument.
Set $4DEF to $2A, revive slot one as type $46 if inactive and derive its position from Arthur's X and $48E5. At coarse region five advance the section. Then run the optional spawn check.
Copy one of two 32-byte sets of properties to $B9A8, selecting the second set from horizontal position $BC onward. Set $4DEF to $FF and call $8EB8.
On phase three, scan six countdown bytes starting at $8C4F. Dispatch $8CA0 when a countdown is zero or decrements to zero. Then call the stage's optional actor routine at $900C.
Six live column positions within their map chunks. At the ends of a 20-tile row the tile writer adjusts the corresponding chunk index.
Six live row indexes into the row offset table. Certain tiles increase or decrease the index.
Six even offsets into the resident map pointer table at $4CF0.
Six signed steps for advancing or reversing the column positions.
Six even lengths for the two halves of each tile pattern. They set the limits on the live pattern index.
Six live indexes into the patterns, each counted up on the outgoing path and down on the returning path.
Six delays checked by the second frame hook. A zero delay lets the corresponding edit run on each eligible phase.
Six values copied to the live countdowns after the initialization runs each edit through a full return.
Six phase flags, each toggled at the end of a run through its tile pattern.
Six low bytes paired with the next table, pointing to the tile edit patterns.
Six high bytes paired with the low bytes at $8C61.
Advance each edit through the outward and return phases and install its delay. Then reset the eight actor spawn positions and their fine offsets.
Resolve the map address from the current chunk, row and column, crossing into an adjacent chunk when necessary. Resolve the pattern pointer, choose a tile from either half and write it to the map.
Advance or reverse the pattern index and change the direction flags at either end.
On eligible pattern steps, use the selected terrain character and direction to choose a vertical row change or a horizontal step.
Paired 31-tile sequences selected by edit zero.
Thirty-one bytes between the end of pattern zero and the start of pattern one. The region begins with zeroes followed by a short alternating tile sequence.
Two 16-entry tile sequences addressed by edit one.
Sixteen zero tile codes before the next pattern pointer.
Two six-entry tile sequences addressed by edit two.
Six zero tile codes between the selected patterns.
Two 19-entry tile sequences addressed by edit three.
Nineteen zero tile codes between the patterns selected by edits three and four.
Two twenty-entry tile sequences addressed by edit four.
Twenty zero tile codes before the tile pattern for the last edit.
Two ten-entry tile sequences addressed by edit five.
Ten tile codes after the last selected pair of sequences. It begins with four zeroes and ends with repeating $98, $97 and $96 values.
Six trailing tile codes from $96 through $98 at the end of the edit data, after both halves of the final selected pattern.

Age unoccupied spawns on the eligible phase and clear entries whose slots have retired. For each free entry call the resident fixed spawn parser, then save any allocated slot and raise its Y coordinate value by ten.
Eight slot indexes, each negative until its corresponding actor has spawned.
Eight eight-byte records. Each starts with a six-byte fixed spawn record and ends with the terminator $FF,$FF. During play the helper at $8F68 changes the leading X fields.
Fine positions at byte four of each eight-byte spawn record. $8F68 advances each by $10 and rolls it over after eight steps.
Eight starting columns copied to the records in reverse order during setup at $8C8C.
Multiply the input index by eight and add $10 to the record's fine position. Advance the coarse position when its fine bits wrap. At columns $87 and $A1 reset the column and return with carry set.

Limit the spawn to coarse regions below two, every 32 values of $BC, a random bit and fewer than four optional actors. Choose the type, initialize a high screen position and set the delay and initial shape.

Require coarse region below nine, no active optional slots and a zero four-bit random sample. Allocate type $3A with a random vertical offset from Arthur and start it from one of the two positions at $9059.
Initial X for each side selected by the random direction bit at $9036.

Section 04 has 22 ordered spawn records. Each six-byte record contains a 16-bit X tile, a 16-bit Y tile, packed sub-tile offsets and the actor ID. The scan at $30B3 advances after allocating the actor.

Section 05 has 2 ordered spawn records. Each six-byte record contains a 16-bit X tile, a 16-bit Y tile, packed sub-tile offsets and the actor ID. The scan at $30B3 advances after allocating the actor.
Section 04 and 05 has 0 optional spawn positions. Each record holds the two tile coordinates and one packed sub-tile byte. The bounded search at $3175 tests visibility and a random condition.
Thirty-two tile properties copied over $B9A8 by $8BF4 below position $BC.
Thirty-two replacement tile properties copied to the same range by $8C01 from position $BC onward.
Look for an exact X match in the three-entry table. On a hit set Arthur's Y from the paired table, discard this return address and jump to the resident contact sampler.
Three coarse X values compared with $FB at $9127.
Three replacement Y values, paired with the exact columns.
Set the IRQ operand at $5D07 to $14 and enter the terrain and actor spawn setup.
Three little-endian start addresses for stage 3 music. The resident stage setter copies the six bytes into index six of the SID song table.
Stage 3 supplies this starting address for voice 1 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Stage 3 supplies this starting address for voice 2 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Stage 3 supplies this starting address for voice 3 of in-game track six. The command stream includes notes, control changes and calls to shared phrases.
Continuation of the stage 3 tune region. Following command targets from its three starting pointers reaches the last phrase bytes at $98A2.
The current packed stage payload includes a byte-for-byte copy of stage 2 music data through $9A51. The three active pointers refer to their own earlier sequence region.
Copied stage 1 stream suffix through $9D01. This copy is reproduced by the disk decoder for this stage.

Loaded 32-byte prefix before the first 200-byte terrain chunk. The entry snapshots share byte $55 followed by zeros. Layout pointers start at $A020.

Use the tile code as the index into the $B6 page selected by $2EEF. $48CC subtracts the selected byte from the player's ground-aligned Y value.
